title: BizFlood Claim Denial Letters — Reasons, Suit Period and Appraisal Notice
content:
A denial of a coverage under BizFlood Commercial Flood Policies (Surplus Lines) is written and states one denial reason: not a flood event, no coverage on the date of loss, proof of loss not timely, location not scheduled, excluded property, or loss below deductible; and it informs the insured that suit may be filed within the tier's suit limitation period in calendar months and that appraisal is available when the tier makes appraisal available.

## Contents of every denial

| Element | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Form | Written |
| Reason | Exactly one of the six reasons below |
| Suit | The insured is informed that suit may be filed within the suit limitation period, in calendar months |
| Appraisal | Where the tier makes appraisal available, the insured is informed that appraisal is available |

## The six denial reasons

1. Not a flood event
2. No coverage on the date of loss
3. Proof of loss not timely
4. Location not scheduled
5. Excluded property
6. Loss below deductible

A denial is made for one coverage of a claim; each denial states one reason from this list and no reason outside it.

## Counting the suit period (hypothetical dates and a hypothetical 24-month period)

A written denial dated 10 October of one year leaves suit open within 24 calendar months, to 10 October two years later.
